title: Bible 6: Basics for a Biblical Worldview
edition: 1st ed., 2021 (Student Edition ISBN 978-1-62856-627-7; Teacher Edition 978-1-62856-628-4 per the work list)

sources.what: publisher Lesson Plan Overview, 1st ed. (unit titles, section numbers, day-by-day topic headings; headings used here)
publisher Biblical Worldview scope and sequence, 2025 (Grade 6 topic strands)
retailer listing confirming BJU Press, 1st Edition, ISBN 9781628566277

summary: BJU Press's grade 6 Bible course: an introduction to worldview built on the Bible's story of creation, fall and redemption and on the categories of structure (how God made things) and direction (whether they are bent toward or away from him). Eight units, 180 lesson days, move from what a worldview is through God, human identity, time and culture, relationships, church, community and government, to how Christians understand and talk with people who hold other worldviews.

toc.label: Unit 1
toc.title: What Is a Worldview?
toc.covers: A worldview's three parts (big story, beliefs driven by loves, actions), assumptions, kinds of proof, the two-story view, and how people make sense of the world.

children.label: Section 1.1
children.title: The Parts of a Worldview; The Thing Everybody Has; Different Glasses; Your Glasses
children.covers: Defines a worldview by its big story, its basic beliefs driven by loves, and its individual and group actions, pictured as lenses.

children.label: Section 1.2
children.title: Big Stories at the Movies; Big Stories People Tell; Evolutionary Glasses; Biblical Glasses
children.covers: How the big story a person believes shapes what they see, comparing an evolutionary story with the biblical one and analyzing secularism.

children.label: Section 1.3
children.title: Bad Assumptions on TV; Bad Assumptions at School; Bad Assumptions about Technology; Bad Assumptions about Society; Good Assumptions
children.covers: Spotting the assumptions carried by media, school, technology and society, and how assumptions shape a worldview.

children.label: Section 1.4
children.title: Proof by Experience; Proof by Authority; Proof in the Bible; The Ultimate Authority, the Ultimate Proof
children.covers: Two main kinds of proof, what counts as evidence, and the Bible as the final authority.

children.label: Section 1.5
children.title: Head and Heart for Me; Love and "Stuff"; Love and Arguments; Love and Stories; Head and Heart for God
children.covers: How what people love drives their beliefs and choices, and loving God with head and heart.

children.label: Section 1.6
children.title: Dualism versus the Bible; The Two-Story View
children.covers: The 'two-story' split between sacred and secular life and why the Bible rejects it, with real-life examples.

children.label: Section 1.7
children.title: Making Sense of the World through a Big Story; Making Sense of the World through Love; Making Sense of the World through Authority; Making Something of the World
children.covers: How story, love and authority, good or twisted, shape the way a person interprets evidence and acts in the world.

toc.label: Unit 2
toc.title: How Should the Bible Shape My Worldview?
toc.covers: The Bible's origin and purpose and its big story of creation, fall, covenants, Christ and redemption, with structure and direction as tools for applying it.

children.label: Section 2.1
children.title: Where the Bible Came From; Why God Gave Us the Bible; Knowing God through His Story; Why We Need the Bible to Know God
children.covers: The history of the English Bible, Scripture as God's story, and why people need the Bible to know God.

children.label: Section 2.2
children.title: God--the Eternal Author; Planning the Good End from the Very Beginning; God--the Author-Creator; The End of God's Story
children.covers: God as author of history who planned its good end from the beginning; the structure of the Bible's story.

children.label: Section 2.3
children.title: God's Very Good Creation; Created in the Image of God; The Creation Mandate; Real Value
children.covers: Creation, humans in God's image, and the Creation Mandate to fill and rule the earth; structure in family, school and work.

children.label: Section 2.4
children.title: The Fall of Adam and Eve; The Curse; The Curse and the Creation Mandate; Blaming God
children.covers: The Fall and the curse, their effect on family, school and work, and a nonbiblical view of death.

children.label: Section 2.5
children.title: Stages in the Bible; God's Covenant with Noah; God's Covenant with Abraham; God's Covenant with Israel through Moses; God's Covenant with David; The Promised New Covenant; The Hero of God's New Covenant--Jesus
children.covers: The biblical covenants as the stages of God's plan, culminating in Jesus.

children.label: Section 2.6
children.title: The First and Second Kings; The Church and the King; Conquering the Citizens; Conquering the Hearts; The King Who Redeems; The King Who Rules
children.covers: The Bible's kingdom theme: the church's role in God's plan while it suffers, Christ as redeeming and ruling King, and final redemption.

children.label: Section 2.7
children.title: Structure and Direction; Living a Redemptive Life; The Biblical Story and Your Desires
children.covers: Telling God-given structure from fallen direction in culture, and pursuing redemptive direction in family, school, work and politics.

toc.label: Unit 3
toc.title: Who Is God, and Why Should I Care?
toc.covers: God's attributes and Trinity, and God as the basis of truth, goodness, beauty and love; God's glory and his involvement with creation.

children.label: Section 3.1
children.title: All These Things; Your Greatest Need and the Bible; What God Is Like; The Attributes of God; The Trinity; How You Should Respond
children.covers: A person's greatest need, God's attributes, and the Trinity.

children.label: Section 3.2
children.title: Truth--for Real; God and Truth; Living Out the Truth
children.covers: Truth grounded in God and why Christians tell the truth.

children.label: Section 3.3
children.title: Good--for Real; Observing Stories; Observing Jesus; God and Goodness; How Your Worldview Handles Evil; God's Moral Standard; God's Solution to Evil; Living Out Goodness
children.covers: Goodness and evil defined from God's character, the problem of evil, and God's solution to it.

children.label: Section 3.4
children.title: Beauty--for Real; Defining Beauty; God and Beauty; God's Truth, Goodness, and Beauty
children.covers: A biblical account of beauty and judging cultural products by it.

children.label: Section 3.5
children.title: Defining Love the Wrong Way; Fuzzy Feelings?; Self-Sacrifice?; Love--for Real; God and Love; A People for His Name; When God's Love Goes Deep
children.covers: Love defined by God's own love rather than by feeling, and how believers show it.

children.label: Section 3.6
children.title: A Bible Study on God's Ultimate End; For Himself; For His Glory; God as All in All; Why God Created You
children.covers: God's glory as the ultimate purpose of creation and of each person.

children.label: Section 3.7
children.title: Seeing from the Highest Pedestal; God, the Bridge Builder; An Involved God; Celebrities
children.covers: God's transcendence and his close involvement with creation, against nonbiblical views of God.

toc.label: Unit 4
toc.title: Who Am I?
toc.covers: Human identity and worth in God's image, the Fall's effect on the self, redemption and union with Christ, and the fight against the flesh, the world and the devil.

children.label: Section 4.1
children.title: Sources of Identity; A Bunch of Identities; Gender Confusion; The Bible and Your Identity
children.covers: Where people look for identity, including the book's treatment of gender identity, set against identity grounded in Scripture.

children.label: Section 4.2
children.title: God and Human Worth; Human Worth and Idols; Your Value
children.covers: Human worth as given by God, and how idols distort it.

children.label: Section 4.3
children.title: Layers of Sin; The Fall and Your Identity; The Fall and Your Desires; Structure and Fallen Direction in You
children.covers: How sin affects identity and desires, and confessing sin to God.

children.label: Section 4.4
children.title: Two Families; Redemption through Adoption; Sanctification; Redeemed Identity; The Gospel
children.covers: Adoption into God's family, sanctification, and a redeemed identity that shapes the response to failure.

children.label: Section 4.5
children.title: Union with Christ; Vine and Branches; Head and Body; Overcoming Sin; If You Love Me
children.covers: Union with Christ pictured as vine and branches and head and body, and love for Christ as the motive for obedience.

children.label: Section 4.6
children.title: The Flesh; Idols of the Heart; Conquering the Enemy Within
children.covers: The flesh and heart idols, and a strategy for opposing them.

children.label: Section 4.7
children.title: Opposition from Without; The Devil; The World; Resisting the Devil and His Kingdom; Love and Fighting
children.covers: Temptation from the devil and the world, and resisting it through prayer.

toc.label: Unit 5
toc.title: How Should I Spend My Time?
toc.covers: The cultural mandate, wisdom and the fear of the Lord, good works and vocation, school, and responding to and creating culture.

children.label: Section 5.1
children.title: The Image of God and the Creation Mandate; The "Cultural" Mandate; Created for Culture
children.covers: The Creation Mandate as a call to develop culture.

children.label: Section 5.2
children.title: Reading for Wisdom; The Fear of the Lord; Becoming Wise in One Lifelong Step; Loving the Best Things
children.covers: Biblical wisdom rooted in the fear of the Lord, and choosing between good, better and best uses of time.

children.label: Section 5.3
children.title: Living Lives of Good Works; Loving Your Neighbor with Your Job; Wisdom and Good Works
children.covers: Good works and loving one's neighbor through ordinary work.

children.label: Section 5.4
children.title: "Because I Said So!"; Because Your Youth Is the Time to Become Wise; Because School Helps You Do Good Works out of Love for Others; Because Submitting Your Life to God Makes You Flourish
children.covers: Reasons from Scripture for taking school seriously.

children.label: Section 5.5
children.title: Different Kinds of Culture; Condemning Culture; Consuming Culture; Critiquing Culture; Copying Culture
children.covers: Ways of responding to culture, including social media, and when each is fitting.

children.label: Section 5.6
children.title: Taking the Next Step; Cultivating Culture; Creating Culture; Now Do It
children.covers: Cultivating and creating culture as a Christian.

children.label: Section 5.7
children.title: Devoted to Good Works; The Good Works of Cultivation and Creation; Influencing
children.covers: Cultivating, creating and influencing as good works.

toc.label: Unit 6
toc.title: How Should I Relate to Others?
toc.covers: Manhood and womanhood, family roles, children's duties, friendship, and the family and society in a fallen world.

children.label: Section 6.1
children.title: God Created Man in His Image; Masculine Character; Special Revelation about Men; General Revelation about Men
children.covers: The book's account of biblical manhood from Scripture and from general revelation.

children.label: Section 6.2
children.title: God Created Woman in His Image; Feminine Character; Special Revelation about Women; General Revelation about Women
children.covers: The book's account of biblical womanhood from Scripture and from general revelation.

children.label: Section 6.3
children.title: Husbands: Loving Leaders; Fathers: Loving Leaders; Wives: Suitable Helpers; Mothers: Instructive Leaders; Your Future
children.covers: The roles the book assigns to husbands, fathers, wives and mothers.

children.label: Section 6.4
children.title: The Biblical Responsibilities of Children; Obeying Your Parents; Honoring Your Parents; Loving Your Siblings; A Biblical Warning to Children; Living Long in the Land
children.covers: Children's duties to obey and honor parents and love siblings, including responding when parents act unbiblically.

children.label: Section 6.5
children.title: Living in Community; What Friendship Is; Finding Friends; Faithful Wounds and Greater Love; Friendship Failures; Friends for Life
children.covers: A biblical view of friendship, including correction and responding to a friend's sin.

children.label: Section 6.6
children.title: What Society Is; Manhood and Womanhood in a Fallen World; The Consequences of Confusion; The Grace of God in Your Family; A Strong Web
children.covers: Society as a web of relationships, the effects of fallen thinking on the family, and strengthening one's own family.

children.label: Section 6.7
children.title: The Presence of Homosexuality; Political Cliques; Social Media Nastygrams; Strengthening the Web; Your Voice in Your Society
children.covers: How the book addresses homosexuality, political factions and online hostility from its biblical-worldview standpoint, and a Christian's voice in society.

toc.label: Unit 7
toc.title: How Should I Fit into Society?
toc.covers: Individual and community, the church, community organizations, government, and Christian citizenship.

children.label: Section 7.1
children.title: Extremes; CFR: The Individual; CFR: The Community; Getting off the Seesaw
children.covers: Avoiding extremes by valuing both the individual and the community ('CFR', probably creation-fall-redemption, is the lens).

children.label: Section 7.2
children.title: Understanding the Church; Universal Church; Local Church; The Mission of the Church; Permitting the Little Children
children.covers: The universal and local church, biblical word pictures of it, and its mission.

children.label: Section 7.3
children.title: Church Membership; What to Look for When You Go to Church; Ways You Can Participate in Church
children.covers: Church membership, evaluating a church biblically, and ways a student can take part.

children.label: Section 7.4
children.title: The Bible and Your Neighbor; Community Organizations; Healthy Communities
children.covers: Loving neighbors through community organizations.

children.label: Section 7.5
children.title: Back to the Basics; Helping Your Neighbors' Physical Needs; Helping Your Neighbors' Spiritual Needs
children.covers: Meeting neighbors' physical and spiritual needs in light of the Creation Mandate and the Great Commission.

children.label: Section 7.6
children.title: Why Government Began; The Fall and Government; Creation and Government; Purposes of Government; Limits on Government; King Jesus and Caesar
children.covers: The origin, purposes and limits of government, and Christ's authority over rulers.

children.label: Section 7.7
children.title: Responsibilities of a Christian Citizen; Virtues of a Christian Citizen
children.covers: A citizen's duties (pray, participate, submit, witness) and virtues (prudence, bold humility, respect).

toc.label: Unit 8
toc.title: How Do I Relate to People with Other Worldviews?
toc.covers: How worldviews and cultures form, then Islam, Buddhism, the religiously unaffiliated ('Nones'), secularism and Moralistic Therapeutic Deism, each compared with the Bible, ending with a personal worldview plan.

children.label: Section 8.1
children.title: The Making of Worldviews; The Idolatry of False Worldviews; The Making of Cultures; Why You Should Understand Different Worldviews; How to Talk to People with Different Worldviews
children.covers: False worldviews as forms of idolatry, and how to understand and talk with people who hold them.

children.label: Section 8.2
children.title: The History of Islam; The Story, Beliefs, and Practices of Islam; The Five Pillars; Different Groups in Islam; Bible Answers to Muslim Beliefs
children.covers: Islam's history, beliefs, Five Pillars and branches, compared with biblical teaching, including the death of Jesus.

children.label: Section 8.3
children.title: The History of Buddhism; The Story, Beliefs, and Practices of Buddhism; Four Noble Truths; The Eightfold Path; The Problem with Desire; Bible Answers to Buddhist Beliefs
children.covers: Buddhism's history and teachings, compared with biblical teaching.

children.label: Section 8.4
children.title: The History of the Nones; Unbelief's Different Belief; The Story, Beliefs, and Practices of Unbelief; Bible Answers to Nones' Beliefs
children.covers: The rise of the religiously unaffiliated and the beliefs implicit in unbelief.

children.label: Section 8.5
children.title: An Example of Secularism; The History of Secularism; The Myth of Secular Neutrality; Bible Answers to the Secular Solution
children.covers: Secularism's history and its claim to neutrality.

children.label: Section 8.6
children.title: The Story, Beliefs, and Practices of MTD; Christianity and MTD; Bible Answers to MTD's Beliefs
children.covers: Moralistic Therapeutic Deism and how it differs from biblical Christianity.

children.label: Section 8.7
children.title: God Gave Me a Good World as a Gift to Enjoy; The World I Live in Demands That I Be Discerning; I Can Thrive in This World with God's Help; I Can Live with Hope That Christ Will Make Everything Right Again; My Worldview Plan
children.covers: Summary convictions for living in the world and writing and presenting a personal worldview plan.

notes: Unit titles and section numbers are BJU's. The Lesson Plan Overview does not print section titles, so each section's 'title' field lists the topic headings BJU gives for that section's lesson days, minus routine items such as 'Section introduction', 'Unit opener' and 'Thinking It Through'. Section boundaries were inferred from where each 'Section introduction' falls; the 6.3/6.4 split, where the overview's layout is jumbled, is the least certain. Each unit ends with a review day and a test (180 days in all). The 2025 BJU scope and sequence also names Hinduism among the worldviews, but the 1st-edition overview shows no Hinduism section. Unit 6 teaches defined roles for men and women and addresses homosexuality and gender identity from a conservative evangelical position. The teacher ISBN 978-1-62856-628-4 comes from the work list and was not checked against a fetched page.
